clue.text: Bad spelling

blocks.note: surface reading: careless orthography, getting the letters of words wrong
setter's reading: the casting of evil spells, sorcery used for harm

explanation.walkthrough: Spelling looks like writing words correctly; here it is the casting of spells, and bad ones at that.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery invoking evil powers is the wicked kind of witchcraft, the opposite of white wizardry.

clue.text: A current measure in beer and scotch

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means its letters sit inside the second

blocks.note: a dark, strong kind of beer
the ampere, unit for measuring electric current

explanation.surface: Someone ordering a pint of beer with a whisky chaser, oddly fussing over electrical units.
explanation.walkthrough: STOUT holds AMP: ST-AMP-OUT. Scotch looks like the whisky but is the verb meaning to put an end to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or rebellion is to crush it decisively, ending it completely.

clue.text: Fruit from East Chile - or China, originally

indicators.note: taken as how the letters were originally arranged before being reordered, a loose signal to rework them

blocks.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grocer debating whether some imported fruit came from Chile or from China.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit is native to southern China, so the Chinese reference is a fair aside; lichee is a variant spelling of lychee.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee is a small sweet tropical produce item with rough red skin and white flesh.

clue.text: Operatic prince to leave in unending anger

indicators.note: without an ending means the last letter is cut off
one thing put in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a literary word for anger
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An opera prince storming off stage in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Ire is a literary word for anger; unending trims its tail before the leaving verb is placed inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is the title hero of Borodin's Russian opera about a twelfth-century campaign.

clue.text: Are they used to keep beehive hairdos in place?

definitions.text: Are they used to keep beehive hairdos in place?

blocks.note: surface reading: the tall back-combed hairstyle of the 1960s, held up with combs

blocks.clueFragment: Are they used to keep beehive hairdos in place?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a real beehive is kept in shape by the wax cells bees build inside it

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is a comb for a beehive hairdo versus the wax comb inside an actual hive.
explanation.definitionFit: The waxy hexagonal cell structures bees build to store nectar give a hive its shape.

clue.text: Such a town has a unique mode of transport

blocks.note: first meaning: a phrase for a small, dull, backward place
second meaning: read literally, a single steed to ride

explanation.surface: A sleepy little place whose only transport is one horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom one-horse town is taken literally, as if the town really owned just a single animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small insignificant settlement is called a one-horse town; literally, one animal is the only conveyance.

clue.text: She made her name in production of Hamlet

indicators.note: a production of a play reworks its material, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actress who became famous playing in Shakespeare's Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Her name is literally made from the letters of Hamlet, which is the cryptic joke behind 'made her name'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a female first name, so a woman can stand in for she.

clue.text: Act in rotation

blocks.note: first meaning: a performer's spot on a variety bill
second meaning: a single circular movement, or a go in sequence

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests performers taking it in rotation; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A music-hall act is called a turn, and spinning round once is also a turn.

clue.text: Dismissing and discussing no further

blocks.note: first meaning: releasing someone from employment
second meaning: dropping a subject and moving on

explanation.surface: A manager firing someone and then refusing to talk about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing staff is a polite phrase of releasing them, and dropping a topic is likewise releasing it.

clue.text: Famous Indian, he comes back in, run out

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word is read backwards
out suggests something disordered, so these letters are scrambled
one thing comes in another, sitting inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous Indian cricketer returns to the crease only to be run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Run out sounds like cricket, a game Indians love, but it signals a jumble of the letters of run.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of independent India, a celebrated national figure.

clue.text: Char with mop out clears away moths

definitions.note: a description of what the answer does rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and laid out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady armed with a mop drives the moths out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is the British word for a cleaning woman, which makes the surface domestic.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor has a strong smell that repels insects, and was the traditional ingredient of mothballs.

clue.text: Troops stepped out in this formation

definitions.text: Troops stepped out in this formation

blocks.note: surface reading: soldiers marched out on parade

blocks.clueFragment: Troops stepped out in this formation
blocks.note: setter's reading: units arranged in a staggered, step-like line, each offset from the next

explanation.walkthrough: Stepped out suggests marching; it actually describes the staircase shape of the formation.
explanation.definitionFit: A military arrangement of parallel units each set back like the rungs of a ladder, from French for ladder.

clue.text: Low quarters of the elk

blocks.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle
south and east, two compass quarters

explanation.surface: The lowly living space of an elk.
explanation.walkthrough: Low looks like an adjective but is the cattle verb; quarters are compass points rather than lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the animal Europeans call an elk is known by this name, the largest deer.

clue.text: Indefinite truce in an engagement

indicators.note: an engagement is a battle, and fighting throws the letters into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ceasefire of no fixed term during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Engagement could mean betrothal, but here it is a military clash shaking up the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not settled or fixed is both vague and doubtful, the two words being close synonyms.

clue.text: It's hell for criminals, generally

blocks.note: first meaning: the realm of the dead below the earth
second meaning: the criminal fraternity as a whole

explanation.surface: A grim view that life is miserable for lawbreakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades lies beneath the earth in myth, and organised crime is the society hidden below respectable life.

clue.text: Those who never do a day's work

definitions.text: Those who never do a day's work

blocks.note: surface reading: idlers who never lift a finger

blocks.clueFragment: Those who never do a day's work
blocks.note: setter's reading: workers whose hours are all after dark

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for lazy people is taken literally: they work, but only through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The team of employees working the overnight hours never work during daylight.

clue.text: For Wagner fans, a godsend?

blocks.note: surface reading: a welcome gift, a blessing
setter's reading: god's end, the downfall of the gods that ends Wagner's Ring cycle

explanation.walkthrough: Godsend is split as gods' end: the German title means Twilight of the Gods.
explanation.definitionFit: The final opera of Wagner's Ring cycle depicts the destruction of the gods and Valhalla.

clue.text: Figures they may be burnt

definitions.note: a description rather than a synonym: things that may be burnt

blocks.note: first meaning: models or images of people
second meaning: what protesters or Bonfire Night crowds set alight

explanation.surface: Accounts or numbers so damning someone may want to burn them.
explanation.walkthrough: Figures suggests numbers; they are images of people, like the Guy burnt on Bonfire Night, the British festival of 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude models representing a disliked person are often set alight as a protest.

clue.text: Such a net may become loose

indicators.note: these words may become something else when their letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fishing net whose mesh may come undone.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose looks like a slack net but means immoral in conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose in the old moral sense describes sexual behaviour lacking virtue or restraint.

clue.text: Boy scouts may sing about them

definitions.text: Boy scouts may sing about them

blocks.note: surface reading: songs whose subject they are

blocks.clueFragment: Boy scouts may sing about them
blocks.note: setter's reading: scouts sit around these at night singing

explanation.walkthrough: About means around, physically, not on the subject of.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor blazes at a camp site are where scouts gather for evening singalongs.

clue.text: Married woman showing ill will

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
a female first name

explanation.surface: A wife displaying resentment, perhaps towards her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or intention to harm someone is a near-exact synonym of hostile feeling.

clue.text: There's money in education

indicators.note: something in a word is contained within it, so the answer sits inside that word

blocks.note: letters two to six of this word

explanation.surface: The cynical observation that schooling can pay well.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a gold coin used across Europe, so it is a historical form of currency.

clue.text: Energetic sort has Monday off

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tireless worker who nevertheless takes Mondays off.
explanation.walkthrough: Off looks like a day off work, but it signals the letters are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful, tireless person is likened to the electrical generator that produces power.

clue.text: Staff instruction to get a move on

definitions.text: Staff instruction to get a move on

blocks.note: surface reading: an order given to employees

blocks.clueFragment: Staff instruction to get a move on
blocks.note: setter's reading: a tempo marking on a musical stave telling players to go briskly

explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like workers but is the five-line musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian tempo direction tells musicians to play quickly and lively.

clue.text: A blue, not with university, shows talent

definitions.note: a verb phrase for an adjective: anyone who shows talent is this

indicators.note: not with means without, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An Oxbridge sporting Blue who, away from the university, still shows talent.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge student who has represented the university at sport; here the word just loses its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Being competent and skilled means having the capacity to do something well.

clue.text: It's inferior to the bean stew

indicators.note: a stew is a mixture cooked up together, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A food critic sniffing that something is worse than a bean stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Stew looks like the dish, but it is the signal to mix up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something below another in rank or worth is lower, or unworthy of it.

clue.text: Lure one into a club

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up inside it

blocks.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Enticing someone into joining a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The club is the sporting bat rather than a society; I goes in after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticement used to attract fish or victims, such as a worm on a hook.

clue.text: Money is a bait that takes many in

indicators.note: with 'in' after the next word, taking in means holding inside

blocks.note: a lure is bait
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: A cynic's view that cash is the bait that catches most people.
explanation.walkthrough: Takes many in also reads as deceives many people, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is a contemptuous phrase for cash, especially gained dishonestly.

clue.text: It's a recurring theme in 16

blocks.note: surface reading: an idea that keeps coming back
setter's reading: the technical German term for a musical tag attached to a character, a device Wagner used throughout the opera at 16

explanation.walkthrough: 16 is the Wagner opera in the grid, whose music is built from these tags.
explanation.definitionFit: A short musical phrase associated with a character or idea, repeated through an opera.
